    Introduction to Exploratory Data Analysis¶

    Based on R for Data Science (R4DS) Chapter 10

    In this notebook we cover:

    • Loading & viewing data with Pandas
    • Visualising variation of numerical and categorical data
    • Intro to Seaborn - a statistical plotting library
    • Visualising covariation between variables

    Generally classified data into types

    • Nominal / Ordinal (Categorical)

    Covariation¶

    If variation describes the behavior within a variable, covariation describes the behavior between variables. Covariation is the tendency for the values of two or more variables to vary together in a related way. The best way to spot covariation is to visualize the relationship between two or more variables.

    Introduction to Seaborn for plotting¶

    Seaborn is a statistical visualisation library, that will make it very easy to visualise categorical/numerical relationships.

    In [19]:
    Copied! 
    # Adjust bin width [0.01, 0.1, 0.5]
BIN_WIDTH = 0.1

df_binned = df_small.copy()
df_binned["carat_bin"] = (np.floor(df_binned["carat"] / BIN_WIDTH) * BIN_WIDTH).round(2)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4))

sns.boxplot(data=df_binned, x="carat_bin", y="price", ax=ax, fliersize=1)
ax.set_xlabel(f"Carat bin, width {BIN_WIDTH}")
ax.set_ylabel("Price")
ax.set_title("Price distribution by carat bin")
ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=90)
plt.show()
    # Adjust bin width [0.01, 0.1, 0.5] BIN_WIDTH = 0.1 df_binned = df_small.copy() df_binned["carat_bin"] = (np.floor(df_binned["carat"] / BIN_WIDTH) * BIN_WIDTH).round(2) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4)) sns.boxplot(data=df_binned, x="carat_bin", y="price", ax=ax, fliersize=1) ax.set_xlabel(f"Carat bin, width {BIN_WIDTH}") ax.set_ylabel("Price") ax.set_title("Price distribution by carat bin") ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=90) plt.show()

    # We can use pandas 'groupby' method to count each cut/color pair

    .reset_index(name="n")
)

cut_color_counts = cut_color_counts.sort_values(["cut", "color"])

    In [23]:
    Copied! 
    # Adjust the kernel density estimate bandwidth to see how this affects visualisation
BW = 1.5

# Turning off the 'common_norm' shows normalised distributions by cut
common_norm = True

cut_order = ["Fair", "Good", "Very Good", "Premium", "Ideal"]

# data: pandas dataframe
# x:    numerical data for density plot
# hue:  categorical input for splitting rows
sns.kdeplot(
    data=df_small,
    x="price",
    hue="cut",
    hue_order=cut_order,
    bw_adjust=BW,
    common_norm=common_norm,
    palette='viridis'
)

plt.xlabel("Price")
plt.ylabel("Density")
plt.title("Price density by diamond cut")
plt.show()
    # Adjust the kernel density estimate bandwidth to see how this affects visualisation BW = 1.5 # Turning off the 'common_norm' shows normalised distributions by cut common_norm = True cut_order = ["Fair", "Good", "Very Good", "Premium", "Ideal"] # data: pandas dataframe # x: numerical data for density plot # hue: categorical input for splitting rows sns.kdeplot( data=df_small, x="price", hue="cut", hue_order=cut_order, bw_adjust=BW, common_norm=common_norm, palette='viridis' ) plt.xlabel("Price") plt.ylabel("Density") plt.title("Price density by diamond cut") plt.show()
